structure.title: A1. Where the check sits in the course (CTH)
structure.html:
• Initial type-rating event: Indoc 7.5 days → aircraft systems ground, 6 days (48 hrs) → systems integration (GFS), 5 days (14 hrs) → 6 crew sim sessions (each 1.0 hr brief, 4 hrs sim, 0.5 hr debrief) → Simulator Check: 2 hrs oral, 4 hrs crew sim check, 1 hr debrief → Simulator LOFT (1 hr brief, 4 hrs sim, 1 hr debrief) [CTH §2.3 p.9].
  • Gate before the sims: "By the end of GFS 5, if you are unable to have the aircraft powered up and ready to taxi in 15 minutes you will not move forward with training" [CTH §16.1 p.69].
  • Who runs the check: "Upon completion of the initial sims and a recommendation for the type check, a Flight Safety Designated Examiner administers the Exam… the check consists of an oral test and a practical test. Satisfactory completion is outlined in the FAA Airman Certification Standards (ACS)" [CTH §16.1 p.69]. ⚠ The paragraph is written for both the SimCom and FSI courses and names FlightSafety. Confirm with SimCom who the examiner will be at Lake Nona.
  • LOFT comes after the type check, flown by a qualified instructor as a typical line segment [CTH §16.1 p.69; §16.3.8 p.80].
  • SimCom trains in a Praetor 600. The CTH says the P500/P600 differences "will not impact flying the simulators." A P500/P600 differences course is the last training requirement [CTH §16.1 p.69].
  • Sim 6 is the practice checkride: practice oral; two precision approaches (Direct Mode only); right-seat cockpit preflight, RTO, gear free-fall, manual RAT deployment; engine start abnormalities; APG special departures; steep turns, stalls, UA; single-engine work; go-arounds / balked landing; system failures; avionics fail-downs; precision, non-precision and raw-data approaches; right-seat takeoff and landing; TCAS and TAWS [CTH §16.3.6 p.79]. The expectation: "Flows, Checklists, Callouts should be satisfactorily accomplished without aids" [CTH p.79].

structure.title: A2. Checking standard
structure.html:
• Checking is conducted to the ACS and FAA Order 8900 guidance. ATP, type rating, 135.293 and 135.297 standards are the same with one key exception: "Retraining for an unsatisfactory task is not allowed during an ATP/TYPE rating certification check" (135.293/.297 does allow retraining and a recheck) [CTH §2.4 p.10].
  • ACS: the evaluator may have you repeat a task that is incomplete or uncertain, but "this provision does not mean that instruction, practice, or the repetition of an unsatisfactory Task is permitted" [ACS App.1 p.62].
  • ACS typical grounds for disqualification [ACS App.1 p.62]:
    • any action or inaction that requires the evaluator to intervene to maintain safe flight
    • failing to clear the area
    • consistently exceeding tolerances
    • failing to take prompt corrective action when tolerances are exceeded
    • failing to exercise risk management
  • In a multi-pilot airplane you are expected to demonstrate CRM [ACS App.1 p.62].
  • Satisfactory performance results in a temporary certificate [ACS App.1 p.62]. The Indoc notes record 120 days for the temporary certificate [NOTES DAY-01.md L46].
  • Tasks required for a multiengine-land type rating [ACS App.1 p.64]:
    • I: A, B
    • II: A, B, C, E
    • III: A, B, I, J
    • IV: all
    • V: all
    • VI: all
    • VII: A, B, D, E, F, G
    • VIII: A
  • Tasks I.C–G (weather, high-altitude aero, air-carrier ops, human factors, CFR) are not required for a type-rating-only applicant [ACS App.3 pp.70–71].
  • Areas IV–VII are performed in actual or simulated instrument conditions, except elements that require visual maneuvering [ACS App.3 p.70].
  • The whole test may be done in a Part 60 FFS within an FAA-approved training program [ACS App.3 p.69].

structure.title: A3. The oral (CTH §2.4.1 + ACS Area I)
structure.html:
CTH oral elements [CTH §2.4.1 p.10]:

  1. Flexjet Immediate Action Items from memory
  2. Aircraft limitations knowledge
  3. Aircraft systems knowledge
  4. Operations: preflight planning · company procedures · OpSpecs · cold weather / anti-icing / de-icing · MEL, CDL · airport ground operations

ACS Area I tasks that apply to a type rating:

  • I.A Operation of Systems (K1–K17):
    • gear and brakes; powerplant; fuel; oil; hydraulics; electrical
    • pneumatic / environmental / O₂ / pressurization; avionics / AP / FMS / EFB / GNSS / SBAS
    • ice protection; crew and pax equipment and evacuation; flight controls; pitot-static
    • fire and smoke; envelope protection (AOA / speed); AFM contents; MEL / CDL
    • Skills include "Recall immediate action items or memory items" (AA.I.A.S2) and "Identify system or component limitations listed in the POH/AFM" (AA.I.A.S3) [ACS pp.2–3].
  • I.B Performance and Limitations:
    • accelerate-stop / go, climb, cruise, descent, landing and OEI performance; W&B
    • icing effects; clean-wing concept, deice / anti-ice, holdover tables, pre-takeoff contamination checks (AA.I.B.K7)
    • compute W&B and CG (AA.I.B.S5–S6) [ACS pp.3–4]
  • ACS App.3: the applicant explains the airplane's systems in the oral, and the evaluator may assess some skill elements in the oral [ACS App.3 p.70].

What the instructors said about the oral:

  • "Knowing your limitations on memory items. That's going to be about at least probably 85% of your oral and then of course add systems on top of that" [IND D3·03-07 37:10–37:20; FLAGS #25]. ⚠ In the transcript, limitations + memory items are ~85% and systems come on top.
  • For the systems questions, "only what you put down on the systems questions is what I'm going to have" (meaning the CTH §7 systems questions) [IND D1·01-01 L785–795].
  • The CTH is "99%" of type prep; use the CFM for flows, profiles and checklist usage [IND D1·01-01 L40–48].
  • Orals are scenario-based around the cockpit poster, a move away from "stump-the-chump"; expect "show me" [IND D1·01-01 L118–139, L160–169; NOTES DAY-01.md L157–167].
  • The P500 and P600 are treated as identical [NOTES DAY-01.md L157–167].
  • Ground icing is a mandatory block on the 8410 form: "I can't pass you [if] I don't check that box" [IND D1·01-01 L776–782; FLAGS #10].
  • Checkride length is roughly 5 hours [IND D1·01-01 L171–181].

structure.title: A4. The practical (CTH §2.4.2)
structure.html:
Expected items (the CTH says "not in any specific order nor a complete listing") [CTH §2.4.2 pp.10–11]:

  • preflight walkaround knowledge · pre-takeoff checks · engine start · ground ops / taxi
  • normal and crosswind takeoffs · instrument takeoff · departure / arrival
  • rejected takeoff · takeoff continued with engine failure above V1 · in-flight engine failure and restart
  • airwork per the CFM training profiles: steep turns; stall recognition and recovery (clean, departure, landing); unusual attitudes
  • 2 precision approaches (ILS, or LPV with DA < 300 ft): 1 hand-flown, 1 single-engine
  • 2 non-precision approaches (LOC, LOC-BC, VOR, LPV with DA > 300 ft, LNAV/VNAV, LNAV, NDB, etc.): 1 hand-flown, 1 from a procedure turn, 1 to a circle
  • two-engine rejected landing (balked landing / go-around) · single-engine go-around · holding · missed approach
  • Landings: single-engine; with 1800 RVR; from a circling approach; from a no-flap condition
  • non-normal and emergency procedures · after landing, shutdown and securing
  • Continuously evaluated: ADM, CRM, company policy / SOP conformity, PM duties

ACS minimums that frame the CTH list [ACS App.3 pp.71–76]:

  • at least 3 landings, 1 to a full stop
  • a briefing before every takeoff and landing
  • 2 different NPAs (one with a course reversal, one from an IAF without AP or vectors, one on backup / partial panel)
  • 2 precision approaches (one without AP, hand-flown from no later than the FAF; one on backup / partial panel)
  • 2 missed approaches (one from a precision approach, one full published missed; in a multiengine airplane, one OEI)
  • a circling approach with at least 90° of total heading change
  • a no-flap / nonstandard-flap landing (required unless the FSBR says otherwise)

maneuversIntro:
How to read each card:

  • ACS = the task code and the exact tolerance text (FAA-S-ACS-11A).
  • CFM = the Flexjet profile callouts. PF calls are orange on the profile, PM calls are green [CFM pp.110–130].
  • ⏳ = numbers that need the AFM/AOM/QRH or the TOLD for the day.

⚠ The profile callouts were transcribed from the CFM profile images (pp.111–130). Spot-check them against the printed CFM before the checkride.

29 maneuver/event cards. The first 27 follow the CTH §2.4.2 order. Card 28 (windshear) is a Sim 5 training item and card 29 is postflight.

maneuvers.title: Preflight walkaround / cockpit preflight
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.II.A: inspect per checklist; document discrepancies and apply MEL/CDL limits; confirm airworthiness; comply with OpSpecs; make sure surfaces are free of ice, snow and frost, and if icing conditions exist, show deicing knowledge (S1–S7) [ACS p.12]. A Part 142 curriculum may use a pictorial preflight [ACS App.3 p.71].
  • CTH: 5 gear/door pins (nose, R main, L main, emergency door, RAT); 21 vortex generators per wing; 17 static wicks [CTH §7.21 p.47].
  • Power-up emphasis [CTH §3 pp.12–13]:
    • HYD pump #1 AUTO, #3 OFF
    • let the electrical PBIT finish
    • if you use the electric pump for brakes (#1 only), let the HYD PBIT finish
    • minimize the time between HYD 3 pump ON and engine start
  • Walkaround checklist items: see Checklists → Walkaround (Aircraft Prep / Walkaround Inspection Rev 3.2).

maneuvers.title: Engine start (normal and abnormal)
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.II.B: ground safety; checklists before and after start; "Respond appropriately to an abnormal start or malfunction" (S4) [ACS p.13]. The evaluator may test start malfunctions by scenario in the oral [ACS App.3 p.71].
  • CFM normal start [CFM pp.79–80]:
    • right engine first, started by the left-seat pilot
    • selector to START for 2 s, then RUN
    • ignition at 1% N2; fuel flow at 10–15% N2
    • stop the clock at 50% N2; call "NORMAL START"
  • CFM manual-abort criteria include: no ITT rise within 30 s; light-off to idle > 50 s; no oil pressure by 30% N2; no N1 by 30% N2 [CFM p.79].
  • CTH: let the FADEC abort a hung start or IGN fail, then run ENGINE ABNORMAL START (QRH NAP1-6) [CTH §8 p.50].
  • Memory: ENGINE ABNORMAL START (the IAI cards).
  • Flows: Before Start (PF) p.40 → After Start (PF p.44 / PM p.45).
  • ⏳ Full QRH NAP1-6 text.

maneuvers.title: Taxi / airport ground operations
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.II.C (taxi) [ACS p.14].
  • CFM: no single-engine taxi (passenger limitations page) [CFM p.82]; taxi in on arrival with two engines [CFM p.96]; pre-taxi briefing is threat-forward [CFM p.78].
  • CTH: pre-taxi briefing per FOM 4.11.1.2 / 4.11.1.3; crosswind ≥ 15 kt → reposition the aircraft into the wind [CTH §3 pp.12–13].
  • Nosewheel steering: ±62° up to 10 kt, ±8° at 25 kt, ±3° at 68 kt; free-castor ±170° [CTH §7.15 p.37].

maneuvers.title: Before-takeoff checks and briefing
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.II.E:
    • determine takeoff performance
    • set speeds and instruments, FD/AP, nav/com
    • brief emergency/abnormal actions (engine failure, windshear) and planned actions (S5)
    • interpret the clearance [ACS p.16]
  • A brief is required before each takeoff; after a satisfactory first brief the evaluator may allow changes-only briefs [ACS App.3 p.71].
  • CFM pre-departure brief, in order [CFM p.77]:
    1. type of takeoff
    2. configuration
    3. V-speeds
    4. abort criteria
    5. initial heading / altitude / fix / SID
    6. emergency plan: EOP and level-off altitude
    7. return plan / takeoff alternate
    8. questions
  • The AWARE brief is done ≥ 30 min before departure; the PIC initiates and the PF leads [CFM pp.76–78].
  • Flow: Before Takeoff (PM) p.52 → Before Takeoff checklist above/below the line pp.53–54, ending with Line-Up Confirmation "RWY__ / CONFIRMED" (PF/PM).
  • CTH initials emphasis: runway heading check at lineup [CTH §3 p.13].

maneuvers.title: Normal and crosswind takeoff
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.III.A: climb speed ±5 kt for each segment (S13); heading ±5° (S14) [ACS pp.18–19]. FFS crosswind is normally 10–15 kt, and the evaluator may go higher up to the AOM/AFM maximum demonstrated [ACS App.3 p.72].
  • CFM takeoff callouts [CFM p.111]:
Event PF PM
Runway clearance "Below the Line" —
Set TO/GA thrust "Check Thrust" "Thrust Set"
Airspeed indicating — "Airspeeds Alive"
80 kt "Checked" "80 knots" (PM verifies the airspeeds match)
V1 − 5 KIAS — "V1"
VR — "Rotate"
Climb "Gear Up" "Positive Rate"
400 ft AGL min "Climb Sequence", "Autopilot" (optional) "400 feet"; selects FMS speeds, VS, flaps up, AP if commanded
  • CFM notes [CFM p.111]:
    • if "HOLD" doesn't annunciate, disconnect the A/T and set thrust manually
    • with no FD: rotate to 12° (flaps 1) / 11° (flaps 2)
  • CFM p.85/86: no FD mode changes below 400 ft AGL; TOGA until at least 400 ft AGL.
  • CFM p.83: After Takeoff checklist not before 3,000 ft AGL or acceleration height; ≤ 1,000 fpm for the last 1,000 ft of a climb.
  • CFM crosswind [CFM p.83]: dry takeoff 35 kt, landing 25 kt demonstrated; takeoff crosswind > 25 kt needs PIC and FODM agreement.
  • Flow: After Takeoff (PM) p.55.
  • ⏳ V1/VR/V2/VFS for the day: TOLD / AFM performance.
  • ⏳ Noise abatement variant: CFM p.112 (V2+15 to 400 ft or boundary; 1,500 ft AFL "1500 ft, VFS" / "Flaps Up"; normal climb at 3,000 ft AFL).

maneuvers.title: Instrument takeoff
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.VI.A:
    • IMC at or before 100 ft AGL; FFS visibility no greater than ¼ mile (S7)
    • make takeoff callouts per operator procedures (S9)
    • heading ±5°, airspeed ±5 kt (S12) [ACS p.37; App.3 p.74]
  • CFM: same callouts as card 5 [CFM p.111].

maneuvers.title: Departure and arrival procedures
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.VI.B (departure): airspeed ±10 kt, heading ±10°, altitude ±100 ft, accurately track (S8) [ACS p.38].
  • ACS AA.VI.C (arrival): airspeed ±10 kt but not below VREF, heading ±10°, altitude ±100 ft (S10) [ACS p.39].
  • CFM p.85:
    • AP on: the PF makes all selections except altitude (the PM sets altitude)
    • hand-flying: the PM makes the selections
    • the PM enters FMS changes in flight and the PF verifies
  • Flows: Transition Altitude p.57 / In-Range p.60.
  • CFM speeds p.94:
    • climb Schedule 2 (P600 250/M0.74; P500 250/M0.72)
    • descent M0.76 → 300 KIAS; max 250 KIAS below 10,000 ft
    • recommended ≤ 200 KIAS at or below 2,500 ft AGL

maneuvers.title: Rejected takeoff
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.III.I: reject when a failure occurs where the airplane can be stopped on the remaining runway (S2); promptly reduce power, use drag and braking (S3); complete procedures, checklists and radio calls (S4) [ACS p.27].
  • CFM RTO profile [CFM p.125]:
    1. "ABORT, ABORT" (PF or PM)
    2. before V1: thrust idle, reversers as required, max braking; PM advises ATC
    3. after the stop: parking brake SET or taxi clear; advise ATC; evacuation memory items if needed, otherwise PA "remain seated"
    4. check the brake cooling charts
  • CTH sequence [CTH §8 p.50; §3 p.13]: PF does the IAIs → PM calls ATC → PF calls for the checklist; then MX / FODM, a new release, revised W&B, and an incident report within 24 hr. "The P600 shows high brake temps."
  • Memory: REJECTED TAKEOFF (At or below V1) (the IAI cards).
  • ⏳ QRH Rejected Takeoff checklist; AFM brake energy / cooling charts.

maneuvers.title: Engine failure above V1 (V1 cut)
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.VII.B:
    • continue the takeoff when able (S3)
    • after the climb is established, airspeed ±5 kt (S4)
    • heading ±5° when the failure occurs (S5)
    • checklists and ATC (S6–S7) [ACS p.50]
  • The failure is given after V1 and before V2, or as close as possible after V1 when V1 = VR [ACS App.3 p.76].
  • The instructor on V1-cut heading: "plus or minus five degrees" [IND D1·01-01 L160–169].
  • CFM Part 1 [CFM p.126]:
    • standard takeoff calls; PM "Engine Failure/Fire"; "V1", "Rotate", "Positive Rate" / "Gear Up"; hold V2 minimum
    • at 400 ft AGL: PM "400 FEET" → PF "FLCH", "HDG (or LNAV)", "1/2 Bank", "Autopilot" (optional)
    • PM "(State Malfunction)" → PF "Call Acceleration Altitude"
  • CFM Part 2 [CFM p.127]:
    • at 1,500 ft AFL or acceleration altitude if higher: PM "Acceleration Altitude"; set VFS
    • at VFS: PM "VFS" → PF "Flaps Up", "1/2 Bank OFF"
    • at MEA/MSA: dial VENR (200 kt)
    • PF "Confirm L/R Engine Failure" → PM "(L/R) Engine (Failure/Fire)"
    • PF "Engine (Failure/Fire) Memory Items" (memory items for fire only) → PM "Memory Items Complete"
    • PF "Engine (Failure/Fire) Checklist" → PM "…Checklist Complete"
    • PF "After Takeoff Checklist"
    • OEI T/O thrust 10 min (normal 5 min)
  • CTH sim tips [CTH §8 pp.50–51]:
    • rudder; don't over-rotate
    • the FD TO mode targets ~V2
    • at 400 ft: HDG/LNAV, FLCH, bug V2, ½ bank
    • acceleration altitude is the minimum safe altitude for checklists
    • don't reduce power in critical situations, even with a fire
    • verify before engine-affecting actions; guard the run switch; no restart after a fire
  • ⏳ QRH checklists: Engine 1(2) Fail EAP6-3, Engine Fire EAP7-2, Engine Shutdown NAP1-27 (names/tabs per [CTH pp.67–68]); single-engine and engine-fire checklists are Sim 6 review items [CTH p.79].

maneuvers.title: In-flight engine failure and restart
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.VII.D:
    • identify the failure and do the memory items (S1)
    • decide whether a restart is viable (S4)
    • keep the operating engine within limits (S5)
    • airspeed ±10 kt, altitude ±100 ft, heading ±10° (S6)
    • restart per procedures (S7) [ACS p.52]
  • In a type-rated airplane the failure may be simulated, but a restart must be considered and a simulated restart performed if applicable [ACS App.3 p.76].
  • CTH: no restart after an engine fire [CTH §8 p.51]. APU in-flight assisted engine start is limited to 23,000 ft [CTH §5 p.17].
  • ⏳ QRH engine relight / in-flight start procedure and AFM start envelope. The CTH §5 p.18 in-flight start ITT figures are listed in (e) as a training reference only.

maneuvers.title: Steep turns
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.IV.A:
    • complete no lower than 3,000 ft AGL (S1)
    • manufacturer's airspeed or ≤ VA (S2)
    • ≥ 45° bank, ≥ 180° by instruments (S3); opposite direction (S4)
    • altitude ±100 ft, airspeed ±10 kt, bank ±5°, rollout ±10° (S6)
    • no impending stall or limit exceedance (S7) [ACS p.30]
    • hand-flown with no PM intervention [ACS App.3 p.73]
  • CFM [CFM p.119]:
    • AP, A/T and FD OFF; clear the FMA
    • clean, trimmed at 200 kt level
    • 45° bank (±5), 200 kt (±10), altitude ±100
    • add about 2–3% thrust and +2° pitch
    • roll out on the assigned heading
    • the PM makes no power or control inputs
    • the instructor may authorize 180° turns
  • CTH: VA ≈ 205–255 KIAS, depending on pressure altitude [CTH §5 p.16].

maneuvers.title: Stall: departure / partial-flap configuration
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.V.A:
    • recovery no lower than 5,000 ft AGL for transport-category airplanes (S1)
    • partial-flap configuration (S3)
    • bank 15–30° manually or with AP (S4)
    • recover at the first indication (S5), per the AFM (S6)
    • retract flaps and gear on a positive rate (S7) [ACS p.33]
  • In an FSTD the entry should be operationally representative, with no minimum entry altitude [ACS App.3 p.73].
  • One stall must be in a 15–30° turn, and one should be commanded through the autopilot [ACS App.3 p.73].
  • Low-airspeed warnings don't count as a stall warning. There's no mandated altitude-loss value and no requirement to hold altitude [ACS App.3 p.73].
  • CFM departure stall [CFM p.120]:
    • gear up, flaps 1, up to 20° bank; AP, A/T and FD off
    • at the first indication PF: "Stall"; lower the pitch / reduce AOA, thrust MAX, confirm speed brakes retracted, level the wings
    • PM "Thrust Set"; PM "TOP OF THE LSA"; PF pitches for minimum altitude loss and resumes the climb
    • PM "F Bug" → PF "Flap Zero" → PM "Flap Zero"; "After Takeoff Checklist"

maneuvers.title: Stall: clean configuration
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.V.B: cruise configuration, 15–30° bank, recover at the first indication, return to the flight path (S1–S7) [ACS p.34].
  • CFM clean stall [CFM p.121]:
    • flaps 0, gear up, AP ON, A/T off; entry 180 KIAS, thrust idle
    • PF "STALL"; "LOW SPEED" cue → max power, lower the nose, level the wings, recover
    • return to the entry altitude and speed
  • ⚠ Ask the instructor: the ACS says a low-airspeed warning "cannot be used as an indication of an impending stall" [ACS App.3 p.73]. Confirm which Praetor cue the examiner treats as the stall warning. The CTH says the DM LSA band Vsa marks "the airspeed at which the stall aural alert is triggered" and the AOA limiter isn't operational in DM [CTH §7.12 p.33]. verify vs AFM/AOM when available (LSA / AOA limiter, stall warning logic in NM).

maneuvers.title: Stall: landing configuration
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.V.C: landing configuration, 15–30° bank, first-indication recovery, retract flaps and gear on a positive rate (S1–S7) [ACS p.35].
  • CFM approach-to-landing stall [CFM p.122]:
    • AP, A/T and FD off; gear down, flaps FULL; entry 150 KIAS at idle
    • PF "STALL"; recover
    • PM "TOP OF LSA" → PF "FLAP 2"
    • PM "POSITIVE RATE" → PF "GEAR UP" → PM "GEAR UP"
    • PM "F BUG" → PF "FLAP ZERO" → PM "FLAP ZERO"
    • return to entry

maneuvers.title: Unusual attitudes
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.IV.B: identify nose-high and nose-low attitudes; apply control, power and configuration in the correct sequence to return to stabilized level flight (S1) [ACS p.31].
  • CFM [CFM p.123]: AP, A/T and FD off.
    • Nose high: increase thrust; roll toward the nearest horizon (up to 60°); nose through the horizon; level; adjust.
    • Nose low: idle; wings level; speed brakes as required; pitch to level; adjust.
    • Don't exceed 60° bank; avoid rolling pull-outs.

maneuvers.title: Holding
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.VI.J:
    • proper entry (S2)
    • cross the fix at or below max holding speed (S3)
    • comply with leg length (S4) and reporting (S5)
    • airspeed ±10 kt, altitude ±100 ft, heading ±10° (S7)
    • use the automation (S8); update fuel reserve for the EFC (S9) [ACS p.47]
  • CTH tip: in the FMS, HOLD TO = course reversal; HOLD AT = hold [CTH §8 p.52].
  • CFM icing: hold at 200 KIAS with gear and flaps up in icing [CFM pp.97–108].
  • FMSG 13-20/13-22: the FMS sizes each circuit for wind and TAS and picks the entry method automatically; the hold fix flashes ~5 s before crossing.

maneuvers.title: Precision approach, hand-flown (ILS / LPV)
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.VI.E:
    • before the FAF: altitude ±100 ft, heading ±5°, airspeed ±10 kt (S9)
    • adjust DA and visibility (S10)
    • FAF → DA: ≤ ¼-scale vertical/lateral, airspeed ±5 kt (S12)
    • go around at DA without the required references (S13) [ACS pp.41–42]
    • the manually flown segment begins no later than the FAF [ACS App.3 p.75]
  • ACS AA.VI.F (landing from precision): ±5 kt and ¼ scale from DA to visual; touchdown −250/+500 ft of the aiming point (S1, S4) [ACS p.43].
  • CFM precision profile [CFM p.113]:
Point PM PF
Course alive "Course Alive" "Flaps 1" (160 KIAS)
Glideslope alive "Glideslope Alive", "Missed Approach Altitude Set" "Gear Down", "Flaps 2" (140 KIAS, within ~10 NM)
1 dot from GS intercept — "Flaps Full", "Before Landing Checklist" (Vapp or Vref + gust; flaps 3 or FULL)
Before every flap move "Speed checks, Flaps selected ___" —
500 ft above DA "500 to Minimums, Stabilized, __ headwind/tailwind" "Stabilized" or "Go Around"
100 ft above DA "100 to Minimums" —
Runway seen early "Runway (or visual reference) __ o'clock" "Visual" or "Continue"
DA "Minimums", "Approach Lights (or Runway) in sight" or "Go Around" "Visual" / "Continue" / "Go Around"
  • CFM notes [CFM p.113]:
    • the PM calls deviations; every "below glidepath" below 1,000 ft AFL gets called
    • the PF must call "Visual" before descending below DA
    • the PM commands a go-around if there's no visual reference
    • flap and speed brake handles are verbally verified
  • CTH tips [CTH §8 p.52]:
    • approach lights only → down to 100 ft above TDZE
    • the PM doesn't call the runway in sight until the threshold lights are in view
  • FD mode guide [CTH §8.3 p.53]: ILS on FMS source = APPR (LNAV→LOC→GS); on V/L source = APPR (LOC→GS); GA ALT set after GS capture. RNP/LPV/LNAV-VNAV = LNAV → VNAV → APPR, GA ALT after GP capture.
  • CFM: don't arm APPR until cleared for the approach [CFM p.85]. ILS APPR only with heading deviation < 90° and within 30 NM [CTH §5 p.19]. LPV requires dual GPS [CTH §5 p.19].
  • ⚠ Indoc conflict: one Indoc instructor said "we don't do a hundred foot call out" [IND D2·02-03 L276–278]. The CFM profile includes "100 to Minimums" [CFM p.113] and governs.
  • Flows: In-Range p.60 → In-Range checklist (incl. LDTA) pp.61–62 → Before Landing pp.63–64.

maneuvers.title: Precision approach, single-engine, manually flown
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.VII.F:
    • before the FAF: altitude ±100 ft, airspeed ±10 kt, heading ±5° (S9)
    • FAF → DA: ≤ ¼ scale, airspeed ±5 kt (S12–S13)
    • go around at DA if not visual (S15) [ACS p.54]
    • begin hand-flying before the final segment; the failure occurs before the final segment [ACS App.3 pp.76–77]
  • CFM: the precision profile applies OEI as well [CFM p.113]. OEI missed approach: see card 22 [CFM p.128].
  • CTH: the go-around FD is a fixed ~8° pitch and doesn't adjust for OEI; pitch ~10–12° for VAC [CTH §8 p.51]. FMS speeds are not approved OEI [CTH §5 p.19].
  • ⏳ QRH single-engine approach and landing checklist; AFM OEI VAC and landing flap.

maneuvers.title: Non-precision approaches (LOC / VOR / LNAV / NDB; one from a procedure turn; one hand-flown; partial panel)
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.VI.D:
    • before the final segment: altitude ±100 ft, heading ±5°, airspeed ±10 kt (S9)
    • adjust MDA/DDA (S10)
    • final segment: ≤ ¼-scale CDI, airspeed ±5 kt, MDA +50/−0 ft to VDP/MAP (S12)
    • missed approach if not visual (S13) [ACS p.40]
  • The course reversal, IAF-without-AP/vectors and partial-panel requirements are in (a) A4 [ACS App.3 pp.74–75].
  • CFM non-precision profile [CFM p.114]:
    • IAF outbound 180 KIAS
    • "Course Alive" / "Flaps 1" (160)
    • PM "Out of __ for __" at every step-down
    • IAF inbound, or 5 NM before the FAF straight-in: "Gear Down", "Flaps 2" (140)
    • established inbound, or 2 NM before the FAF: "Flaps Full", "Before Landing Checklist" (Vapp)
    • FAF: "Out of __", "TIME"
    • "500 / 100 to Minimums"
    • MDA: PM "Minimums, (time or distance) to go" or "Runway __ o'clock"; PF "Continue" / "Visual"; PM "Missed Approach Altitude Set"
    • MAP: PM "Runway in sight" or "Missed Approach Point (Go Around)"
    • the PF must call "Visual" before circling or descending below MDA
  • CFM approach configuration [CFM pp.90–93]:
    • LP not authorized (Collins limitation)
    • LNAV is flown LNAV + VNAV without pressing APPR (AFM 2-64 p.7)
    • for VOR/NDB the ground navaid is the final authority
  • CTH FD guide p.53 / tips p.52:
    • LOC = select LOC (not ILS) → LNAV (LOC) + FPA; set GA ALT if using the MDA as a DDA, otherwise set the MDA
    • VOR/NDB on FMS source = LNAV + FPA
    • LNAV-only minima use NAV mode
    • VOR/NDB need the RMI needle (bearing source)
    • SBAS can be deselected via IDX ARR DATA
  • verify vs AFM/AOM when available (approach/navigation limitations) full text.

maneuvers.title: Circling approach and landing
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.VI.G: airspeed ±5 kt, heading/track ±5°, altitude +100/−0 ft until descending below MDA (S5) [ACS p.44].
  • ACS AA.VI.H: bank ≤ 30° (S4); ±5 kt, +100/−0 ft (S5); touchdown −250/+500 ft (S8) [ACS p.45].
  • The runway may be < 90° offset if you make at least 90° of total heading change [ACS App.3 p.75].
  • CFM circling [CFM p.117]:
    • flown like the NPA; max 30° bank; Vapp or Vref + gust minimum
    • PF "Leaving Minimums"
    • PM calls headwind/tailwind at or below 500 ft AGL once aligned
    • at MDA the PM sets the missed approach altitude
  • Circling category: all Flexjet aircraft circle as CAT C (P500 CAT B / P600 CAT C) [CTH §5 p.19; CFM pp.90–93].
  • FD guide: use HDG after reaching the MDA; set the MDA for circling, and GA ALT after reaching the MDA [CTH §8.3 p.53].

maneuvers.title: Missed approach (two engines)
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.VI.I:
    • prompt initiation and a report to ATC (S1)
    • flaps/gear in sequence; airspeed ±5 kt (S3)
    • heading/course ±5°, altitude ±100 ft (S7)
    • re-engage the AP when appropriate (S10) [ACS p.46]
    • a momentary dip below DA while initiating at DA is not unsatisfactory if it doesn't continue [ACS App.3 pp.75–76]
  • CFM missed approach [CFM p.116]:
    • "Go Around" (either pilot) at DA/MAP
    • PF: TO/GA, thrust to the T/O detent, pitch for VAC
    • PM: verifies T/O power, selects flaps 2 (flaps 1 if landing flaps were 3), calls "Flaps 2"
    • "Positive Rate" / "Gear Up"
    • PM "400 FEET" → PF "Select Manual Speed to MAX", "Autopilot" (optional), "FMS SPEEDS"
    • After Takeoff checklist at 3,000 ft AFL minimum or the initial level-off
    • notes: a flaps-0 approach stays flaps 0; no FD → 12°/11°
  • CFM p.85 / CTH p.52: press TOGA to sequence the missed approach.
  • FMSG 13-47: the approach is disabled by TOGA, by selecting AUTO when the TO waypoint is the MAP, or by deleting the FAF.

maneuvers.title: Single-engine missed approach / go-around
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.VI.I: one missed approach must be OEI [ACS App.3 p.75]. AA.III.J: positive climb, airspeed ±5 kt (S3) [ACS p.28].
  • CFM OEI missed approach [CFM p.128]:
    • as card 21, but at 400 ft: "FLCH", "HDG (or LNAV)", "½ Bank", "Autopilot"
    • acceleration altitude → "VFS" / "Flaps Up", "½ Bank OFF"
    • VENR 200 at MEA/MSA
    • After Takeoff checklist at 3,000 ft AFL minimum or level-off
  • ⏳ QRH OEI go-around flap setting / AFM OEI climb limits.

maneuvers.title: Two-engine rejected landing (balked landing)
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.III.J:
    • timely decision (S1); power and pitch (S2)
    • airspeed ±5 kt (S3); configure (S4)
    • track (S6); checklists (S7) [ACS p.28]
    • initiated about 50 ft above the runway, approximately over the threshold; may count as one of the 3 landings [ACS App.3 p.72]
  • CFM: as the missed approach profile [CFM p.116].

maneuvers.title: Normal landing / landing with 1800 RVR / visual approach
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.III.B:
    • configuration and airspeed ±5 kt (S7)
    • touchdown on centerline at −250/+500 ft of the aiming point (S10)
    • taxi speed (≤ 20 kt dry / ≤ 10 kt contaminated) within the calculated landing distance + 25% (S12)
    • go around if not within tolerance (S14) [ACS p.19]
  • ACS stabilized approach: stable speed, descent rate and path; configured by the minimum stabilized height, e.g. 1,000 ft AAE at ≤ 1,000 fpm [ACS App.3 p.74]. CTH/FOM: ≤ 1,000 fpm in the last 1,000 ft (FOM 4.13.8) [CTH §12 p.59].
  • CFM landing [CFM p.95 and profile p.115]:
    • 50 ft at adjusted VREF on a 3° path, gear down, flaps 3 or FULL
    • the ATS currently retards at 30 ft, so VAPP = VREF + 5
    • reversers DEPLOYED at nosewheel touchdown
    • PM calls "40" (40 KIAS)
    • profile p.115: at 500 ft AGL (or 500 ft above minimums IFR) the PM confirms the wind is within limits; TRs stowed by 40 KIAS
  • CFM gust factor: added to VREF [CFM p.96].
  • CFM autobrake [CFM p.96]: PIC discretion; disengage at 80 kt; OFF for emergency/abnormal procedures.
  • CFM visual [CFM p.118]:
    • downwind flaps 1 = 160
    • abeam 140, "Gear Down Flaps 2"
    • base: minimum Vapp, "Flaps FULL, Before Landing Checklist"
    • final turn complete by 500 ft AFL; "500, Stabilized, wind"
  • CTH: visual default is 5 mi / 3° [CTH §8 p.52].
  • Flows: After Landing (PM) p.65, done after clearing the runway. No switches until clear of the runway [CFM p.96].

maneuvers.title: Single-engine approach and landing
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.VII.E:
    • before the FAF: altitude ±100 ft, airspeed ±10 kt, heading ±5° (S6)
    • approach ±5 kt (S7)
    • touchdown −250/+500 ft (S10); after-landing checklists (S13) [ACS p.53]
    • "follow the manufacturer's recommended procedures" [ACS App.3 p.77]
  • ⏳ QRH One Engine Inoperative Approach and Landing Checklist NAP1-39 [CTH pp.67–68]: text, flap setting and VREF adds.

maneuvers.title: No-flap / partial-flap landing
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.VII.G: calculate speeds (S4); stabilized approach (S5); touchdown at the agreed point −250/+500 ft (S8); stop (S10) [ACS p.55].
  • CFM no-flap / partial-flap profile [CFM p.129]:
    • 2.5–3° path; control speed with thrust
    • speed brakes down to 160 kt; fly it onto the runway
    • 182 kt max tire speed; firm touchdown; max reverse
    • pattern 200 KIAS (see the flap-fail checklist for airspeed)
    • PF "Gear Down, Before Landing Checklist"; 500 ft "Stabilized" call
  • ⏳ QRH Flaps Fail EAP8-4 [CTH pp.67–68; Sim 6 list p.79]: VREF adds and landing-distance factors.

maneuvers.title: Emergency procedures (incl. emergency descent, fire/smoke, decompression, evacuation, icing)
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.VII.A:
    • explain and perform emergency procedures including emergency descent, in-flight fire and smoke, decompression, emergency evacuation, airframe icing, and others from the AFM (S1–S2f)
    • fly on standby instruments (S3)
    • checklists (S4); ATC (S5) [ACS p.49]
  • CFM emergency descent [CFM p.124]:
    • PF "CABIN ALTITUDE HI Warning Checklist" → IAIs (same as memory) → PF "Emergency Descent"
    • the PM runs the Emergency Descent checklist
    • leveling at 10,000 ft or MEA: retract speed brakes, set thrust, masks off at 10,000 ft if not required, advise pax
    • if structural damage is suspected, limit speed and loads
  • CFM checklist order [CFM p.16]: memory items → emergency → abnormal → normal.
  • CFM p.17: the PF calls the IAIs and the PM performs them in coordination; use the Flexjet laminated normal checklist when the QRH says go to normal.
  • CFM p.15: only the Emergency/Abnormal ECL is approved; if the ECL revision doesn't match TechPubs, use the QRH.
  • Memory items: SMOKE EVACUATION, SMOKE/FIRE/FUMES, CABIN ALTITUDE HI, EMERGENCY DESCENT, ENG 1/2 FIRE, APU FIRE, CARGO SMOKE, etc. (the IAI cards).
  • ⏳ QRH checklists: Emergency Descent, Smoke/Fire/Fumes, Smoke Evacuation, Cabin Altitude Hi, Evacuation, PFD Failure, Hydraulic Pressure Low, FLTCTRL Direct Mode, Electrical Emergency (QRH refs the CTH names: Engine Abnormal Start NAP1-6, Engine 1(2) Fail EAP6-3, Engine Shutdown NAP1-27, OEI Approach & Landing NAP1-39, Engine Fire EAP7-2, Flaps Fail EAP8-4 [CTH pp.67–68]). ⏳ Max cabin altitude / emergency-descent specifics (open item [NOTES open-items.md]).

maneuvers.title: Windshear (training item, Sim 5)
maneuvers.html:
• ACS: the takeoff briefing must cover windshear (AA.II.E.S5) [ACS p.16].
  • CFM windshear recovery [CFM p.130]:
    • PF "Windshear Recovery": thrust MAX, AP DISENGAGE, pitch 15° initially, then toward minimum airspeed while respecting the LSA/PLI; configuration MAINTAIN
    • PM "MAX Power set"
    • target ~10 kt above the low-speed cue
    • PM calls airspeed, pitch, vertical speed and altitude; notify ATC when able
    • no flap or gear change until clear; then "Gear Up", "Flaps Up", "After takeoff checklist"
  • ⚠ CTH: windshear detection SB 550-34-0003 is NOT INSTALLED [CTH §6 p.21]. The IAI "WINDSHEAR WITH FD ESCAPE MANEUVER" is titled "(Airplanes equipped with Windshear Detection System)" [MEM]. Ask how the sim will present windshear and which procedure applies.

maneuvers.title: After landing, parking, securing
maneuvers.html:
• ACS AA.VIII.A: runway incursion avoidance; checklists after clearing the runway; park; postflight; secure (S1–S6) [ACS p.57].
  • CFM:
    • After Landing flow p.65; After Landing silent checklist p.66
    • Shutdown flow p.67: the left seat observes a minimum 3 minutes before the run switches go OFF
    • Shutdown checklist p.68; Securing pp.69–70
    • BITE: power down 15 min [CFM p.75]

flowRules.title: C1. Rules of the road [CFM pp.12–17]
flowRules.html:
• Flows are memorized, and a flow is not challenge-response [CFM p.12].
  • Checklist replies:
    • "AS REQUIRED" is never an acceptable checklist response. State the actual position or condition, e.g. "Anti-ice is ON" [CFM p.13]
    • completion call: " COMPLETE", e.g. "TAXI CHECKLIST COMPLETE" [CFM p.14]
    • after the flows, the PF calls for the checklist [CFM p.12]
  • Interrupted checklist: "Hold the checklist at …" / "Continue the checklist" [CFM p.14].
  • ◆ marks a first-flight-of-day item [CFM p.15].
  • Only the Emergency/Abnormal ECL is approved. If the ECL revision doesn't match TechPubs, use the QRH [CFM p.15].
  • No skipping items. The After Takeoff checklist is done at 3,000 ft AGL minimum [CFM p.16].
  • Priority: memory items → emergency → abnormal → normal [CFM p.16].
  • The PF calls the IAIs and the PM performs them in coordination. When the QRH says go to the normal checklist, use the Flexjet laminated normal checklist [CFM p.17].
  • Automation [CFM p.85]:
    • AP ON: the PF makes selections except altitude (the PM sets altitude)
    • hand-flying: the PM makes selections
    • no FD mode changes below 400 ft AGL
    • don't arm APPR until cleared
    • TOGA sequences the missed approach
  • ½ bank [CFM p.85]: automatic above 25,000 ft; not used in terminal areas except for an engine failure.
  • Instructor goal for startup: "should be 20 min" (a crew took an hour) [IND D1·01-01 L171–181]. GFS 5 gate: powered up and ready to taxi in 15 min [CTH p.69].

Where a flow or checklist line reads "AS REQ", say the actual setting out loud; "AS REQUIRED" is never an acceptable response [CFM p.13].

Checklists that follow each flow (challenge/response):

  • Before Start pp.41–43; After Start pp.46–48; Departure/Runway Change pp.49–51
  • Before Takeoff pp.53–54, above/below the line:
    • above the line: Brakes/Steering; TAKEOFF CONFIG (TO CONFIG button); FUEL X-FEED OFF; Brake Temp; Departure Briefing
    • below the line, after runway clearance, on PF "continue below the line": Auto-Throttle (ARMED or OFF); Lights; EICAS; HDG/LNAV; Line-Up Confirmation "RWY__ / CONFIRMED"
  • After Takeoff (silent) p.56; Transition/Cruise p.58; Descent p.59
  • In-Range pp.61–62: includes LDTA COMPLETED/CHECKED, TOLD card, approach briefing
  • Before Landing pp.63–64: includes Landing Gear "DOWN, 3 GREEN" (PM & PF); Flaps SET/INDICATED
  • After Landing (silent) p.66; Shutdown p.68; Securing pp.69–70; Traffic Pattern pp.71–73

memoryDrill:
Master copy: MEMORY-ITEMS (word-for-word from CTH Rev 2.5 §4 pp.14–15). The IAI cards on this site use that exact wording (machine-checked, not retyped). Never paraphrase an IAI [MEM header].

  • The CTH says IAIs "may be evaluated during any training or checking event" [CTH §4 p.15]. They're the first CTH oral element [CTH §2.4.1 p.10] and an ACS skill (AA.I.A.S2).
  • Titles to recite on demand (22 items, verbatim titles):
    • SMOKE: SMOKE EVACUATION · SMOKE/FIRE/FUMES · CARGO SMOKE
    • NON-ANNUNCIATED: DUAL ENGINE FAILURE · EMERGENCY DESCENT · ENGINE ABNORMAL START · ENGINE SEVERE DAMAGE OR SEPARATION · FLTCTRL N-MODE MISBEHAVIOR · JAMMED SIDESTICK · GEAR LEVER CAN NOT BE MOVED UP
    • (2) AMS: CABIN ALTITUDE HI
    • (5) ELECTRICAL: BATT DISCHARGING · > ELEC EMERGENCY
    • (7) FIRE PROTECTION: APU FIRE · ENG 1 FIRE · ENG 2 FIRE
    • (8) FLIGHT CONTROLS: > FLTCTRL N-MODE FAIL · SIDE STICK LH (RH) FAIL
    • (12)/(13): LG WOW MISCOMPARE · A-I WINGSTAB LEAK
    • SOPM: WINDSHEAR WITH FD ESCAPE MANEUVER · REJECTED TAKEOFF
  • Rev 2.5 change: "Added immediate action item LG WOW MISCOMPARE" (Highlights of Revision) [CTH p.8].
  • Drill method:
    1. Write each one out blind.
    2. Diff it against the IAI cards.
    3. Say it with the switch-touch ("show me") the instructors expect [IND D1·01-01 L160–169].
    4. Pair each with its trigger (the EICAS message, or the black-banner non-EICAS condition) [MEM legend].
  • Look-alike pairs to drill (wording copied from MEM):
    • CABIN ALTITUDE HI and EMERGENCY DESCENT have the same five lines. The only print difference is "10000 ft" vs "10,000 ft".
    • ENG 1 FIRE / ENG 2 FIRE vs ENGINE SEVERE DAMAGE OR SEPARATION: the same four actions, with "(affected engine)" wording in the latter.
    • SMOKE EVACUATION = SMOKE/FIRE/FUMES + "OXYGEN Selector ··· CREW ONLY" + "DUMP Button ··· PUSH IN".
    • Three items end in "PITCH Switch ··· ACTUATE MANUALLY": FLTCTRL N-MODE MISBEHAVIOR, > ELEC EMERGENCY, > FLTCTRL N-MODE FAIL. LG WOW MISCOMPARE ends in "PITCH SWITCH ··· ACTUATE MANUALLY".
  • ⚠ The OCR stored "MAEUVER" as MANEUVER; confirm against the printed CTH if challenged [MEM note].
  • ⏳ The follow-on QRH checklist text after each IAI: QRH.

  • initials only: checklist philosophy, AWARE, flight-instrument check (After Start flow), Before Takeoff brief, runway heading check at lineup, turnaround / traffic-pattern checklists, dry motor
qaIntro: Self-authored from the sources above only; every answer is cited. Tags: PROGRAM ACS MEM FLOWS CALLOUTS SOP LIMITS SYS-… OPS. Items tagged LIMITS or SYS that rely on the CTH are training reference, verify vs AFM/AOM verify vs AFM/AOM when available.

qa.q: What are the pieces and durations of the initial Simulator Check?
qa.a: 2 hr oral, 4 hr crew sim check, 1 hr debrief. LOFT follows the type check. [CTH §2.3 p.9; §16.1 p.69]

qa.q: You fail a task on the type ride. Can the examiner retrain you and recheck it on the spot?
qa.a: No. Retraining an unsatisfactory task isn't allowed on an ATP/TYPE certification check; 135.293/.297 does allow it. [CTH §2.4 p.10; ACS App.1 p.62]

qa.q: List the CTH oral exam elements.
qa.a: Flexjet IAIs from memory; aircraft limitations; aircraft systems; operations (preflight planning, company procedures, OpSpecs, cold weather / anti-ice / de-ice, MEL/CDL, airport ground ops). [CTH §2.4.1 p.10]

qa.q: What must you be able to do by the end of GFS 5 to move on?
qa.a: Have the aircraft powered up and ready to taxi in 15 minutes. [CTH §16.1 p.69]

qa.q: What precision approaches does the CTH expect on the check?
qa.a: Two, ILS or LPV (DA < 300 ft): one hand-flown and one single-engine. [CTH §2.4.2 p.11]

qa.q: What non-precision approach events does the CTH list?
qa.a: Two NPAs: one hand-flown, one from a procedure turn, one to a circle. [CTH §2.4.2 p.11]

qa.q: Which landings are listed?
qa.a: Single-engine; with 1800 RVR; from a circling approach; from a no-flap condition. [CTH §2.4.2 p.11]

qa.q: What four things are evaluated continuously throughout the check?
qa.a: ADM, CRM, company policy/SOP conformity, pilot-monitoring duties. [CTH §2.4.2 p.11]

qa.q: Steep turn standard?
qa.a: At least 45° bank for at least 180°; altitude ±100 ft, airspeed ±10 kt, bank ±5°, rollout ±10°. [ACS AA.IV.A.S3, S6] The CFM flies it at 200 kt clean with AP/A/T/FD off. [CFM p.119]

qa.q: Non-precision final-segment tolerances?
qa.a: ≤ ¼-scale CDI, airspeed ±5 kt, MDA +50/−0 ft to the VDP or MAP. [ACS AA.VI.D.S12]

qa.q: Precision approach tolerances, FAF to DA?
qa.a: ≤ ¼-scale deflection of vertical or lateral guidance and airspeed ±5 kt. Before the FAF: altitude ±100, heading ±5°, airspeed ±10. [ACS AA.VI.E.S9, S12]

qa.q: Engine failure after V1: heading and airspeed tolerances?
qa.a: Heading ±5° when the failure occurs; airspeed ±5 kt once the climb is established. [ACS AA.VII.B.S4–S5; IND D1·01-01 L160–169]

qa.q: Circling approach tolerances and bank limit?
qa.a: Airspeed ±5 kt, heading/track ±5°, altitude +100/−0 ft until descending below MDA; bank no more than 30°. [ACS AA.VI.G.S5; AA.VI.H.S4] The CFM also gives 30° max. [CFM p.117]

qa.q: Touchdown point tolerance on landings?
qa.a: Within −250/+500 ft of the aiming-point markings (750–1,500 ft from the threshold if there are no markings). [ACS AA.III.B.S10; AA.VI.F.S4]

qa.q: Holding tolerances?
qa.a: Airspeed ±10 kt, altitude ±100 ft, heading ±10°; cross the fix at or below max holding speed; update fuel reserves for the EFC. [ACS AA.VI.J.S3, S7, S9]

qa.q: Where is the go-around / rejected landing normally initiated?
qa.a: About 50 ft above the runway, approximately over the threshold. Instrument conditions need not be simulated below 100 ft. [ACS App.3 p.72]

qa.q: In the stall tasks, can a low-airspeed alert count as the stall cue? Must you hold altitude?
qa.a: No: a low-airspeed warning isn't a stall warning. There's no predetermined altitude-loss value and no requirement to maintain altitude. [ACS App.3 p.73]

qa.q: Stall task setup requirements?
qa.a: One stall in a 15–30° turn, and one should be induced through autopilot commands. Transport-category recovery no lower than 5,000 ft AGL (in the airplane); in an FSTD, an operationally representative entry. [ACS AA.V.A.S1, S4; App.3 p.73]

qa.q: Instrument takeoff requirements?
qa.a: IMC at or before 100 ft AGL, FFS visibility ≤ ¼ mile; heading ±5°, airspeed ±5 kt. [ACS AA.VI.A.S7, S12]

qa.q: How many missed approaches, and of what type?
qa.a: Two: at least one from a precision approach, and one full published missed. In a multiengine airplane, one must be OEI. [ACS App.3 p.75]

qa.q: You start the go-around at DA and the airplane sinks a little below DA. Unsatisfactory?
qa.a: No, as long as the descent below DA/DH doesn't continue. [ACS App.3 pp.75–76]

qa.q: What does the ACS define as a stabilized approach?
qa.a: Stable speed, descent rate and vertical path; configured and on speed/power/path before the minimum stabilized height (e.g., 1,000 ft above airport elevation, ≤ 1,000 fpm unless briefed). [ACS App.3 p.74]

qa.q: Which two IAIs have the same five action lines?
qa.a: CABIN ALTITUDE HI and EMERGENCY DESCENT. Recite both from the IAI cards. [MEM]

qa.q: Which IAI was added in CTH Rev 2.5?
qa.a: LG WOW MISCOMPARE. [CTH Highlights of Revision p.8]

qa.q: Name the IAIs in the SMOKE group.
qa.a: SMOKE EVACUATION, SMOKE/FIRE/FUMES, CARGO SMOKE. [MEM]

qa.q: How does SMOKE EVACUATION differ from SMOKE/FIRE/FUMES?
qa.a: It adds "OXYGEN Selector ··· CREW ONLY" and "DUMP Button ··· PUSH IN". [MEM]

qa.q: Which IAIs end with the PITCH switch actuated manually?
qa.a: FLTCTRL N-MODE MISBEHAVIOR, > ELEC EMERGENCY, > FLTCTRL N-MODE FAIL, and LG WOW MISCOMPARE. [MEM]

qa.q: Jammed sidestick: what's the IAI, and what does the long press do?
qa.a: Cross-side AP/PTY button, press and hold for more than 20 seconds [MEM]. Holding AP/PTY for more than 20 s latches priority. [CTH §7.12 p.32]

qa.q: Recite the Before Start flow.
qa.a: Parking Brake SET · Thrust Levers IDLE · Lower DU Status Page VERIFY (All Doors Closed) · Red BCN ON · Hydraulic 3 Electric Pump ON. [CFM p.40]

qa.q: When does the PM do the Before Takeoff flow, and what's in it?
qa.a: On takeoff or LUAW clearance: Brake Temp CHECK · Fuel X-Feed OFF · Lights ON (taxi and strobe; landing when cleared for takeoff) · EICAS CHECK. [CFM p.52]

qa.q: What must be verified before starting the After Start flow, and who does which part?
qa.a: HYD PBIT complete. The PF does ELEC EMER check through EICAS check; the PM does the electrical synoptic, sets flight instruments, checks the flight-control synoptic, and checks flight controls after the PF. [CFM pp.44–45]

qa.q: Shutdown: how long must the left seat observe before the run switches go OFF?
qa.a: A minimum of 3 minutes (Clock 3 Minutes in the flow). [CFM p.67]

qa.q: Is "AS REQUIRED" an acceptable checklist response?
qa.a: Never. State the actual position or condition (e.g., "Anti-ice is ON"). [CFM p.13]

qa.q: How do you pause and resume a checklist?
qa.a: PF: "Hold the checklist at "; then "Continue the checklist". The PM resumes by repeating the last completed item. [CFM p.14]

qa.q: Emergency checklist priority order?
qa.a: Memory items → emergency → abnormal → normal. [CFM p.16]

qa.q: Which electronic checklist is approved, and what if its revision doesn't match TechPubs?
qa.a: Only the Emergency/Abnormal ECL; if the revision doesn't match, use the QRH. [CFM p.15]

qa.q: With the autopilot on, who makes the FCP selections and who sets altitude?
qa.a: The PF makes all selections except altitude, which the PM sets. When hand-flying, the PM makes the selections. [CFM p.85]

qa.q: Lowest height for FD mode changes after takeoff, and how do you sequence the missed approach?
qa.a: No FD mode changes below 400 ft AGL; press TOGA to sequence the missed approach. [CFM p.85; CTH §8 p.52]

qa.q: When does the PM call "V1"?
qa.a: At V1 − 5 KIAS. [CFM p.111]

qa.q: What happens at 80 knots on the takeoff roll?
qa.a: The PM calls "80 knots" and confirms the airspeeds match; the PF responds "Checked". [CFM p.111]

qa.q: What's the 500-ft call on a precision approach, and what are the PF's options?
qa.a: PM: "500 to Minimums, Stabilized, __ headwind/tailwind." PF: "Stabilized" or "Go Around". [CFM p.113]

qa.q: What must the PF announce before descending below DA or MDA (or circling)?
qa.a: "Visual". [CFM pp.113–114]

qa.q: Engine failure after V1: what are the PF's calls at 400 ft?
qa.a: "FLCH", "HDG (or LNAV)", "1/2 Bank", "Autopilot" (optional), after the PM's "400 FEET". [CFM p.126]

qa.q: At acceleration altitude and then VFS on a V1 cut?
qa.a: PM "Acceleration Altitude" (set VFS); at VFS, PM "VFS" → PF "Flaps Up", "1/2 Bank OFF". Venr 200 kt at MEA/MSA. [CFM p.127]

qa.q: On the go-around, what flap setting does the PM select?
qa.a: Flaps 2, or flaps 1 if the landing flap was 3. A flaps-0 approach stays at 0. [CFM p.116]

qa.q: RTO: who can call it, and what's the call?
qa.a: Either pilot: "ABORT, ABORT". [CFM p.125]

qa.q: After an RTO, what follow-up is required?
qa.a: Call MX / the company (FODM), get a new release, revise W&B, and file an incident report within 24 hr. [CTH §3 p.13; §8 p.50; §12 p.59]

qa.q: VAPP vs VREF on a normal landing: why the +5?
qa.a: The ATS currently retards at 30 ft instead of 50 ft, so 5 kt is added to VREF and that becomes VAPP. [CFM p.95]

qa.q: Autobrake: when must it be OFF, and when do you disengage it on landing?
qa.a: OFF for emergency and abnormal procedures; disengage at 80 kt with the pedals. [CFM p.96; CTH §5 p.18]

qa.q: Crosswind limits: demonstrated takeoff and landing, and the company contaminated limit?
qa.a: Takeoff 35 kt, landing 25 kt demonstrated; above 25 kt on takeoff needs PIC + FODM agreement; company contaminated limit 15 kt (use the most restrictive). [CFM pp.83, 96]

qa.q: Flexjet VFE?
qa.a: F1 200, F2 175, F3 175, FULL 160 KIAS; max altitude for flap extension 20,000 ft. [CFM p.95; CTH §5 p.16] verify vs AFM/AOM when available

qa.q: VMO/MMO?
qa.a: 300 KIAS to 10,000 ft; 320 KIAS 10,000–29,475 ft; 0.83 M above. [CTH §5 p.16] verify vs AFM/AOM when available

qa.q: P600 MTOW and MLW?
qa.a: 42,858 lb / 37,479 lb (P500: 37,567 / 34,172). [CTH §5 p.16] verify vs AFM/AOM when available

qa.q: Max tailwind, runway slope, takeoff/landing altitude?
qa.a: 10 kt; ±2%; −1,000 to 9,600 ft (HALTO not installed). [CTH §5 p.16; §6 p.21] verify vs AFM/AOM when available

qa.q: OEI ITT limits?
qa.a: 955 °C steady (10 min), 970 °C transient (2 min); max continuous 950 °C. [CTH §5 p.18] verify vs AFM/AOM when available

qa.q: Autopilot minimums?
qa.a: Engage 400 ft; use 80 ft with a vertical path reference, 180 ft without (AOM 2-56). [CTH §5 p.18; §7.13 p.36] verify vs AFM/AOM when available

qa.q: What powers the aircraft in an electrical emergency, and what's left for displays?
qa.a: An electrical emergency is loss of both main gens and the APU gen in flight. The RAT deploys and powers EMER BUS 1/2/3 and charges the batteries; the CTR DU and ADS 3 remain. [CTH §7.6 pp.25–26; §7.1 p.22; §7.19 p.45]

qa.q: What does pushing the engine fire SHUTOFF button do, and which bottle do you use first?
qa.a: Closes the fuel, hydraulic and bleed SOVs and arms Bottle A and B (both illuminate red). Use Bottle A first to save B, which also covers the APU. [CTH §6 p.20; §7.8 p.28]

qa.q: Why can HYD system 3 work on battery or RAT, and what does the PTU do?
qa.a: Sys 3 is a DC motor pump powered from EMER BUS 3. The PTU transfers power between Sys 1 and 2, automatically on an engine or EDP failure (or manually). [CTH §6 p.20; §7.11 p.31]

qa.q: When is manual reversion to Direct Mode inhibited, and is the AP available in DM?
qa.a: Inhibited while low-speed, AOA-limiter or high-speed protection is engaged. The AP isn't available in DM. [CTH §7.12 pp.31–34] verify vs AFM/AOM when available

qa.q: What is EDM, and when is it enabled and activated?
qa.a: An automatic descent to a safe altitude for depressurization plus pilot incapacitation. Enabled with the AP engaged above 25,000 ft; activates on a red CABIN ALTITUDE CAS. [CTH §7.13 p.35]

qa.q: What triggers ATTCS?
qa.a: If armed, on takeoff or go-around: OEI detected (N2 difference > 15%), loss of engine cross-communication, windshear detected, or a thrust lever to MAX. [CTH §7.10 p.30]

qa.q: Definition of icing conditions, and when does AUTO ice protection activate after takeoff?
qa.a: OAT (ground) or TAT (flight) ≤ 10 °C with visible moisture. AUTO activates above 1,700 ft AGL or after 2 minutes airborne, whichever comes first. [CTH §7.17 pp.40–41]

qa.q: When must the pre-takeoff contamination check be done, and under which OpSpec is it authorized?
qa.a: Within 5 minutes before takeoff (FOM 7.3.7.2), under OpSpec A041. [CTH §12 p.60; §3 p.13; FLAGS #9] ⏳ FOM

qa.q: What are the MEL repair category intervals?
qa.a: A = as stated in Remarks; B = 3 consecutive calendar-days; C = 10; D = 120, each excluding the day of discovery. A single extension is allowed only for B and C (OpSpec D095). [MEL Rev 14 pp.23, 25–26]

qa.q: What must the crew determine before doing an (O) procedure?
qa.a: The item is deferrable per the MEL; the discrepancy won't affect flight safety; the required alternate equipment is operative; and the PIC briefs the SIC. [MEL Rev 14 p.29]

qa.q: When may a flight crew perform an (M) procedure?
qa.a: When the item's Flight Crew Deferral Item column says YES, after coordinating with Maintenance Control. [MEL Rev 14 p.30; CTH §12 p.59]

qa.q: When can the NEF list be used, and what are NEF items?
qa.a: Only if MEL/CDL relief isn't available. NEF items have no effect on safe operation, aren't required by certification or operating rules, and aren't already in the MEL/CDL. [NEF banner pp.1–6; MEL p.25; MEL 25-2]

melIntro:
Sources:

  • MEL = Flexjet MEL, Legacy 450/Praetor 500 (EMB-545) · Legacy 500/Praetor 600 (EMB-550), Rev 14, 02-17-26, 306 pp. Front-matter printed page = PDF page; chapter pages cited as printed "chapter-page".
  • NEF = Flexjet NEF lists: "Legacy 450/500 and Praetor 500" page updated 12/01/2025, Universal list updated 08/26/2026.

Why it matters: MEL/CDL is a CTH oral element [CTH §2.4.1 p.10] and an ACS skill: "Demonstrate or describe… the process for deferring inoperative equipment (e.g., MEL) and using a CDL" (AA.I.A.S4; K17) [ACS p.2–3].

mel.title: I1. How the MEL is built
mel.html:
• Two sections [MEL TOC; pp.1–2]:
    • Section One: equipment items by ATA chapter
    • Section Two: CAS Message Relief
    • then the CDL
  • The MEL is "no less restrictive than" MMEL Rev 6 (12/20/2022) [MEL front matter / TOC summary].
  • The MEL must not deviate from AFM limitations, emergency procedures or ADs. All airworthiness/operating-rule equipment not listed must be operative [MEL Preamble p.31].
  • MEL conditions don't relieve the operator of determining the aircraft is safe. An airworthiness release / logbook entry is required before operating with inoperative equipment [MEL Preamble p.31].
  • With multiple inoperative items, consider how they interact and the effect on crew workload [MEL Preamble p.32].
  • System page columns [MEL Definitions p.26]:
    • item number, item, repair category, number installed, number required for dispatch, remarks or exceptions
    • Section Two adds the CAS message and dispatch consideration
  • Proviso = conditions that must be met. NOTE = information, not part of the proviso [MEL p.26].

mel.title: I2. (M) and (O) procedures
mel.html:
• (M): a specific maintenance procedure accomplished before operation with the item inoperative, normally by maintenance [MEL Definitions p.27].
  • (O): a specific operations procedure for planning or operating with the item inoperative, normally by the flight crew [MEL p.27].
  • Before any (O) procedure, the crew determines [MEL Procedures p.29]:
    1. the item is deferrable per the MEL
    2. the discrepancy won't affect the safety of the flight
    3. the required alternate equipment is operative
    4. with a two-pilot crew, the PIC briefs the SIC on the procedure
  • Flight Crew Deferral Item column [MEL p.30]:
    • "YES" → crews are qualified/authorized for all procedures of that item, and may perform (M) procedures after coordinating with Maintenance Control
    • "NO" → Maintenance must defer it
    • the crew may always ask Maintenance to defer
    • crews are authorized for all Section Two CAS-relief procedures
  • Company Q&A: a crew may only perform an MEL procedure if it says "Flight Crew Deferral Item = Yes" [CTH §12 p.59].
  • Placards go on or adjacent to the inoperative control/indicator. Write the item up at the end of that flight; defer (if permitted) and placard unless corrected [MEL Procedures p.29; Definitions p.25].

mel.title: I3. Repair categories [MEL Definitions pp.25–26]
mel.html:
Cat Interval
A as specified in Remarks/Exceptions (calendar/flight-day intervals exclude the day of discovery; other intervals start at deferral)
B 3 consecutive calendar-days (72 hr), excluding the day of discovery
C 10 consecutive calendar-days (240 hr), excluding the day of discovery
D 120 consecutive calendar-days (2,880 hr), excluding the day of discovery
  • Continuing Authorization – Single Extension (OpSpec D095): a one-time extension for B or C only, not A or D [MEL p.23].
  • Flight-day = a midnight-to-midnight 24 hr period in Eastern time with at least one flight initiated [MEL p.24].

mel.title: I4. Key definitions to know [MEL pp.23–27]
mel.html:
• Inoperative = doesn't accomplish its intended purpose or isn't consistently within limits/tolerances. Considered inoperative = treat it as inoperative for dispatch/taxi/flight; don't use it; placard it; comply with the (M)/(O) procedures and the repair category.
  • Operative (no need to verify) vs Verified operative (must check at the stated interval, or at deferral if no interval is given).
  • EICAS and dispatch [MEL p.24]:
    • any WARNING or CAUTION affects dispatch (use the AFM + MEL)
    • ADVISORY status messages that indicate a failure (e.g., FMS 1 fail) also require the AFM + MEL
    • ADVISORY information and maintenance ("Maintenance Required") messages don't affect dispatch
  • Contaminated runway (MEL definition) = > 25% of the surface covered by frost, ice, any depth of snow, slush or water [MEL p.23].
  • Icing conditions / visible moisture definitions [MEL pp.24, 27]. Compare the CTH icing definition in (f).

mel.title: I5. Two worked examples (checkride-relevant)
mel.html:
• 22-30-00 Autothrottle [MEL 22-9]:
    • Takeoff Hold Mode (Cat C) may be inop if the A/T isn't engaged for takeoff: (O) set the TO/GA detent manually.
    • Retard Mode (Cat C) may be inop if the A/T is disengaged at or above 100 ft before landing: (O) "Disengage auto throttle at or above 100 ft (ONE HUNDRED call out)", retard manually to IDLE at 50 ft.
    • Flight Crew Deferral: YES.
    • (Note: this MEL text also refers to a "ONE HUNDRED" callout; see the (g) G11 conflict.)
  • 30-81-00 Ice Detection [MEL 30-9]:
    • one of two may be inop if the wing/stab and engine anti-ice are operated manually; (O) ENG at OAT 5–10 °C with visible moisture, ALL below 5 °C; in flight ALL when TAT < 10 °C with visible moisture
    • both may be inop only if the airplane is not operated into known or forecast icing
    • Cat C; Flight Crew Deferral: YES

mel.title: I6. NEF concept
mel.html:
• Definition: equipment and furnishings with no effect on safe operation and not required by certification or operating rules. Not items already in the MEL/CDL [MEL Definitions p.25].
  • MEL 25-00-00-01, Nonessential Equipment and Furnishings: "May be inoperative, damaged, or missing provided that the item(s) is deferred in accordance with the operator's NEF deferral program" (the FLEXJET NEF Program). (M)/(O) procedures, if required, must be available to the flight crew. Flight Crew Deferral: YES [MEL 25-2].
  • Every NEF page carries the banner: "ONLY TO BE USED IF MEL/CDL RELIEF IS NOT AVAILABLE" [NEF pp.1–6].
  • Columns: item #, description, ATA, deferral interval (days), PAX convenience item, procedures, restrictions [NEF p.1].
  • Examples:
    • LG008 FMS Navigation Database Expired: 10 days; crew refers to the FOM for procedures [NEF p.1]
    • LG010 Lavatory Door: 30 days; door secured open on aircraft with the emergency exit in the lav [NEF p.1]
    • LG005 RAT Safety Pin/Cover Missing or Damaged: 10 days [NEF p.1]
  • ⏳ FLEXJET NEF Program document (procedures/authority) and FOM MEL policy sections: not on file.

⚠ This is a 2019 vendor guide, so it may lag the installed software. The Flexjet CFM governs SOP, and the AFM governs limitations. The CTH lists the operator's guide P/N 523-0818863 as required to be immediately available whenever navigation relies on the FMS [CTH §5 p.18].

  • Approach guidance sources: FMS lateral guidance always uses GNSS position (even without SBAS) unless the GNSS fails or is deselected. Vertical guidance is always Baro-VNAV, except SBAS VNAV for LPV [FMSG 13-33].
  • "The FMS must not be used for navigation below the MDA or DA." The MDA shown on the ROUTE (LEGS) format is the highest value in the database for that approach; the pilot must determine the correct altitude and set the MDA alerters [FMSG 13-33].
  • Missed approach: the approach can be disabled before the MAP by pushing TOGA, selecting AUTO when the TO waypoint is the MAP, or deleting the FAF. The vertical deviation is removed when the MAP sequences [FMSG 13-47]. Consistent with "TOGA required to sequence the missed approach" [CTH §8 p.52; CFM p.85].
  • Holding: the FMS sizes each circuit from wind and the lower of TAS or MAX HOLD speed, picks the entry method automatically, and extends the parallel-entry outbound leg to stay within protected airspace [FMSG 13-20]. The fix flashes ~5 s before each crossing, and FAA/ICAO max holding speeds are programmed [FMSG 13-22]. Flexjet usage: HOLD TO = course reversal; HOLD AT = hold [CTH §8 p.52].
  • Related Flexjet limits (verify vs AFM): LP not authorized (Collins limitation) [CFM pp.90–93]; GPS-only approaches need predictive RAIM; no baro-VNAV with a remote altimeter setting; LPV requires dual GPS; FMS speeds not approved OEI [CTH §5 p.19].

sections.title: DRY MOTORING PROCEDURE
text: (REF: AOM DATA) Engine starts 15−180 min following engine shutdown.

CAUTION: IF ENGINE RESTART IS DESIRED BETWEEN 15 AND 180 MINUTES AFTER AN ENGINE SHUTDOWN, IT IS RECOMMENDED DRY MOTORING THE ASSOCIATED ENGINE PRIOR TO START FOR 15 SECONDS OR UNTIL N2 REACHES 23%, WHICHEVER OCCURS FIRST. AFTER COMPLETION OF THIS PROCEDURE, A NORMAL ENGINE START SEQUENCE CAN BE INITIATED ANY TIME AFTER 3 MINUTES AND BEFORE 40 MINUTES HAVE ELAPSED.
1. ENG IGNITION Knob (both engines) .................................. OFF
2. IGN OFF Status Icon (both engines).............................. CHECK
3. ENG 2 Start/Stop Knob ...... START (2 SECONDS), THEN RUN Perform the dry motoring for 15 seconds or until N2 reaches 23%, whichever occurs first.

sections.title: HP CART START
sections.intro: It is the PICs duty to ensure the area is clear behind the airplane before utilizing this checklist to start the engines. Bringing the engines to 80% N2 can cause damage to the airplanes, personnel, and buildings behind the immediate area of the engines.

items.note: Verify GPU AVAIL in WHITE is illuminated on the Electrical Panel prior to Pushing In the GPU Button. GPU Button should then illuminate IN USE in Green.
Once ready for engine starts continue below.
NOTE: The PACK button lights will turn on, indicating that the pack inlet valve is closed
The BLEED buttons lights will turn on, indicating that the bleed valve is closed
Check pressure indication between 32 PSI and 60 PSI on STATUS Synoptic Pages.
Perform an engine crossbleed start on the second engine. Next Page.

sections.title: ENGINE CROSSBLEED START
sections.intro: CAUTION: Do not utilize this checklist without first completing the above Legacy 450/Praetor 500 HP Cart Start Procedure.

items.note: Wait a minimum of 3 minutes before advancing the throttle above ground idle. The minimum recommended engine N2 prior to start is 80%
A white light should be illuminated on the button.
NOTE: If APU bleed is available, the pneumatic system logic prioritizes it.
NOTE: An N2 drop at the operating engine is expected, but no thrust lever adjustment is necessary. CAUTION: PERFORM AFTER START CHECKLIST BELOW BEFORE CONTINUING TO NORMAL PROCEDURES CHECKLIST
Respect the warmup time operating the started engine at or near IDLE for at least 3 minutes.
The AIR CONDITIONING/PNEUMATIC Panel should be dark.
Verify White AVAIL in not illuminated on the electrical panel.
Continue with Normal Procedures checklist from this point forward, until another HP cart engine start is required.

bulletins.subject: Hydraulic fluid low quantity associated with hydraulic low press and spoiler fault
bulletins.reason: To inform operators about a procedure when the >HYD 1 (2) LO PRESS CAS Message is displayed together with HYD 1 (2) LO QTY CAS Message.
bulletins.background: Embraer received a report of HYD 2 LO QTY followed by >HYD 2 LO PRESS and SPOILER FAULT. The right-wing midboard multi-function spoiler oscillated due to hydraulic pressure oscillations. The low quantity came from a hydraulic leak; the oscillation came from a malfunction in the multi-function spoiler system.
bulletins.action: Whenever the >HYD 1 (2) LO PRESS CAS Message is displayed together with HYD 1 (2) LO QTY CAS Message, pilots must close the associated Hydraulic EDP by pressing EDP 1 SHUTOFF Button or EDP 2 SHUTOFF Button after completing the >HYD 1 (2) LO PRESS procedure. This step is necessary regardless of the SPOILER FAULT CAS Message being displayed to prevent the possible multi-function spoiler oscillatory movement.
bulletins.cite: OB P550-001/23 pp.1–2 (identical text in OB 550-001/23 except effectivity)
bulletins.pending: The >HYD 1 LO PRESS and >HYD 2 LO PRESS procedure pages (OB pp.3–4) are images and were not extracted. Use the OB pages or the QRH.
drill: Which two CAS messages together trigger the OB action?
>HYD 1 (2) LO PRESS together with HYD 1 (2) LO QTY.
What extra step does the OB add, and when?
Close the associated EDP (EDP 1 or EDP 2 SHUTOFF button) after completing the >HYD 1 (2) LO PRESS procedure.
Do you wait for SPOILER FAULT before doing it?
No. It is required regardless of the SPOILER FAULT message, to prevent possible multi-function spoiler oscillation.
